Questions marked "practice" are NCERT-style questions of a repeating type; no board year is claimed for them.

title: Q1 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q1. (MCQ, 2024)  A function f : R⁺ → R (R⁺ = non-negative reals) is defined by f(x) = 4x + 3. Then f is: (A) one-one but not onto (B) onto but not one-one (C) both (D) neither.    Answer: (A).  f(x1) = f(x2) gives x1 = x2, so one-one. Range is [3, ∞), not all of R, so not onto.

title: Q2 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q2. ★ (A-R, 2025)  Assertion (A): f : Z → Z, f(x) = 3x - 5 is a bijection. Reason (R): A function is a bijection if it is both one-one and onto.    Answer: (D) A is false, R is true.  For y = 0, 3x - 5 = 0 gives x = 5/3, not an integer. So f is not onto, hence not a bijection.

title: Q3 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q3. ★ (5 marks, 2018 type; also 2026)  Show that R = {(a, b) : a, b ∈ A, |a - b| is divisible by 4} on A = {x ∈ Z : 0 ≤ x ≤ 12} is an equivalence relation. Find the set of elements related to 1.    Answer:      Reflexive: |a - a| = 0, and 0 is divisible by 4. So (a, a) ∈ R for all a ∈ A.   Symmetric: if (a, b) ∈ R, then |a - b| = 4k. Now |b - a| = |a - b| = 4k, so (b, a) ∈ R.   Transitive: if (a, b), (b, c) ∈ R, then a - b = ±4k and b - c = ±4m. Adding: a - c = 4(±k ± m), divisible by 4. So (a, c) ∈ R.   Hence R is an equivalence relation.   Elements related to 1: |1 - b| divisible by 4, so b = 1, 5, 9. The set is  {1, 5, 9} .

title: Q4 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q4. ★ (5 marks, 2026)  R = {(x, y) : |x - y| is divisible by a prime number p, x, y ∈ Z}. Check whether R is an equivalence relation.    Answer:  Reflexive: |x - x| = 0 = p × 0. Symmetric: |y - x| = |x - y|. Transitive: x - y = pk and y - z = pm give x - z = p(k + m).  R is an equivalence relation.

title: Q5 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q5. (4 marks, 2020)  On N × N, (a, b) R (c, d) if and only if ad = bc. Show R is an equivalence relation.    Answer:  Reflexive: ab = ba, so (a, b) R (a, b). Symmetric: ad = bc gives cb = da, so (c, d) R (a, b). Transitive: ad = bc and cf = de. Multiply: adcf = bcde. Cancel cd (non-zero, natural numbers): af = be, so (a, b) R (e, f).  Equivalence relation.

title: Q6 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q6. (Case study, 2025)  On A = {1, 2, 3}: R1 = {(2,3), (3,2)}, R2 = {(1,2), (1,3), (3,2)}, R3 = {(1,2), (2,1), (1,1)}, R4 = {(1,1), (1,2), (3,3), (2,2)}, R5 = {(1,1), (1,2), (3,3), (2,2), (2,1), (2,3), (3,2)}. (i) Which is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric? (ii) Which is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive? (iii)(a) Which are symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive? (iii)(b) What pairs must be added to R2 to make it an equivalence relation?    Answer:  (i)  R4  ((1,2) is there but (2,1) is not). (ii)  R5  ((1,2), (2,3) are there but (1,3) is not). (iii)(a)  R1 and R3  (R1: (2,3), (3,2) but no (2,2); R3: (2,1), (1,2) but no (2,2)). (iii)(b) Add  (1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (2,1), (3,1), (2,3) .

title: Q7 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q7. (5 marks, SQP 2026-27 VI version)  R : (-∞, ∞) → [0, ∞), R = {(x, y) : y = x² + 7}. Is it a function? Is it one-one, onto, bijective?    Answer:  Each x gives exactly one y = x² + 7, so it is a  function . f(1) = f(-1) = 8, so  not one-one . y = 0 (in co-domain) gives x² = -7, no real x; range is [7, ∞) ≠ [0, ∞), so  not onto . Hence  not bijective .

title: Q8 · Chapter 1: Relations and Functions
text: Q8. (2 marks, 2019 type)  Show f : N → N, f(x) = x² + x + 1 is one-one but not onto.    Answer:  If f(a) = f(b): a² + a = b² + b gives (a - b)(a + b + 1) = 0. Since a + b + 1 > 0, a = b:  one-one . f(1) = 3 is the smallest value, so 1 and 2 have no pre-image:  not onto .

title: Q10 · Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
text: Q10. ★ (2 marks, 2018)  Find tan⁻¹√3 - cot⁻¹(-√3).    Answer:  tan⁻¹√3 = π/3. cot⁻¹(-√3) = π - cot⁻¹√3 = π - π/6 = 5π/6. Answer = π/3 - 5π/6 =  -π/2 .

title: Q11 · Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
text: Q11. ★ (2 marks, 2025)  Evaluate tan⁻¹[2 sin(2 cos⁻¹(√3/2))].    Answer:  cos⁻¹(√3/2) = π/6. So 2 cos⁻¹(√3/2) = π/3, sin(π/3) = √3/2, and 2 × √3/2 = √3. tan⁻¹√3 =  π/3 .

title: Q12 · Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
text: Q12. (Case study parts, 2024)  (i) Find sin⁻¹(-1/2) - sin⁻¹(1). (ii) Find the domain and range of f(x) = 2 sin⁻¹(1 - x).    Answer:  (i) -π/6 - π/2 =  -2π/3 . (ii) Need -1 ≤ 1 - x ≤ 1, so 0 ≤ x ≤ 2:  domain [0, 2] . sin⁻¹ gives [-π/2, π/2], times 2:  range [-π, π] .

title: Q13 · Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
text: Q13. (MCQ, practice, type of 2020)  Principal value of tan⁻¹(tan 3π/4) is: (A) 3π/4 (B) -π/4 (C) π/4 (D) -3π/4.    Answer: (B).  tan 3π/4 = -1 and tan⁻¹(-1) = -π/4 (must lie in (-π/2, π/2)).

title: Q14 · Chapter 2: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
text: Q14. (MCQ, 2025)  The graph shown is y = cos x on [0, π] (decreasing from 1 to -1). Its inverse graph is the curve from (-1, π) to (1, 0).    Answer:  The graph of  cos⁻¹x : domain [-1, 1], range [0, π], decreasing, passes through (0, π/2). (In the 2025 paper this was option C.)

title: Q15 · Chapter 3: Matrices
text: Q15. (MCQ, SQP)  A = [[2, 1, -2], [3a, 0, 4], [b, 2c, 1]] is symmetric. Then √(6a + 2b + 3c) is: (A) -2 (B) 2 (C) ±2 (D) 4.    Answer: (B).  Symmetric means aᵢⱼ = aⱼᵢ: 3a = 1, b = -2, 2c = 4. So 6a + 2b + 3c = 2 - 4 + 6 = 4, √4 = 2.

title: Q16 · Chapter 3: Matrices
text: Q16. (MCQ, 2026)  If A and B are skew-symmetric matrices of the same order, which is also skew-symmetric? (A) AB (B) AB + BA (C) (A + B)² (D) A - B.    Answer: (D).  (A - B)ᵀ = Aᵀ - Bᵀ = -A + B = -(A - B).

title: Q18 · Chapter 3: Matrices
text: Q18. (MCQ, 2025)  A is 3×3, B is 3×1, C is 1×3. Which products are defined: AB, AC, BA?    Answer: Only AB.  (3×3)(3×1) works. AC needs 3 = 1 (no). BA needs 1 = 3 (no).

title: Q19 · Chapter 3: Matrices
text: Q19. (3 marks, SQP)  P = [[2, 0, 0], [0, 1, 2]] and Q = [[1, 0], [0, 2], [1, 0]]. Find PQ and QP, and the inverse of the product if it exists.    Answer:  PQ = [[2, 0], [2, 2]] (2×2). |PQ| = 4 ≠ 0, so (PQ)⁻¹ = (1/4)[[2, 0], [-2, 2]] = [[1/2, 0], [-1/2, 1/2]]. QP = [[2, 0, 0], [0, 2, 4], [2, 0, 0]] (3×3). Rows 1 and 3 are equal, so |QP| = 0:  inverse does not exist .

title: Q20 · Chapter 3: Matrices
text: Q20. (3 marks, type of 2026C)  Express A = [[3, 5], [1, -1]] as the sum of a symmetric and a skew-symmetric matrix.    Answer:  Aᵀ = [[3, 1], [5, -1]]. P = ½(A + Aᵀ) = ½[[6, 6], [6, -2]] = [[3, 3], [3, -1]] (symmetric, Pᵀ = P). Q = ½(A - Aᵀ) = ½[[0, 4], [-4, 0]] = [[0, 2], [-2, 0]] (skew-symmetric, Qᵀ = -Q). P + Q = [[3, 5], [1, -1]] = A.

title: Q21 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q21. ★ (MCQ, 2020)  A is a square matrix of order 3 and |A| = 5. Then |2A| = ?    Answer: 40.  |kA| = kⁿ|A| = 2³ × 5.

title: Q22 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q22. ★ (MCQ, 2025)  A is of order 2 and det A = 4. Then det(4 adj A) = ? (A) 16 (B) 64 (C) 256 (D) 512.    Answer: (B).  |4 adj A| = 4² × |adj A| = 16 × |A|²⁻¹ = 16 × 4 = 64.

title: Q23 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q23. (MCQ, 2023)  A is 3×3 and |adj A| = 64. Then |A| = ?    Answer: ±8.  |adj A| = |A|² = 64.

title: Q24 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q24. (MCQ, SQP)  P and Q are of the same order, P = [[2, 1], [0, 1]] and |Q| = 3. Find |adj(PQ)|.    Answer: 6.  For 2×2, |adj M| = |M|. |PQ| = |P||Q| = 2 × 3 = 6.

title: Q26 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q26. ★ (5 marks, 2025)  A school puts 180 students into Sports, Music and Drama clubs. Sports = Music + Drama. Music = (half of Sports) + 20. Find the numbers using the matrix method.    Answer:      Let S, M, D be the numbers. Equations: S - M - D = 0; -S + 2M = 40 (from M = S/2 + 20); S + M + D = 180.   A = [[1, -1, -1], [-1, 2, 0], [1, 1, 1]], B = [0, 40, 180]ᵀ.   |A| = 1(2 - 0) + 1(-1 - 0) - 1(-1 - 2) = 2 - 1 + 3 =  4 .   adj A = [[2, 0, 2], [1, 2, 1], [-3, -2, 1]].   X = (1/4) adj A × B: S = (0 + 0 + 360)/4 = 90; M = (0 + 80 + 180)/4 = 65; D = (0 - 80 + 180)/4 = 25.    Sports 90, Music 65, Drama 25.

title: Q27 · Chapter 4: Determinants
text: Q27. ★ (Case study 4 marks, SQP)  Basket A: 5 kg apples, 10 kg oranges, 5 kg pomegranates, cost ₹2750. Basket B: 10, 10, 5 kg, cost ₹3500. Basket C: 8, 15, 7 kg, cost ₹4100. (i) Write the matrix equation and find adj of the coefficient matrix. (ii) Find the price per kg of each fruit.    Answer:      (i) Let x, y, z = price per kg of apple, orange, pomegranate. A = [[5, 10, 5], [10, 10, 5], [8, 15, 7]], X = [x, y, z]ᵀ, B = [2750, 3500, 4100]ᵀ, AX = B.   adj A = [[-5, 5, 0], [-30, -5, 25], [70, 5, -50]].   (ii) |A| = 5(70 - 75) - 10(70 - 40) + 5(150 - 80) = -25 - 300 + 350 =  25 .   X = (1/25) adj A × B: x = (-13750 + 17500 + 0)/25 = 150; y = (-82500 - 17500 + 102500)/25 = 100; z = (192500 + 17500 - 205000)/25 = 200.    Apples ₹150/kg, oranges ₹100/kg, pomegranates ₹200/kg.

title: Q28 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q28. ★ (A-R, 2025)  A: f(x) = 3x - 8 for x ≤ 5 and 2k for x > 5 is continuous at x = 5 for k = 5/2. R: f is continuous at a if LHL = RHL = f(a).    Answer: (D).  f(5) = 15 - 8 = 7 and RHL = 2k. 2k = 7 gives k = 7/2, not 5/2. A is false, R is true.

title: Q29 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q29. (2 marks, practice; type of 2023, 2026, 2026C)  Find k if f(x) = kx + 1 (x ≤ 5) and 3x - 5 (x > 5) is continuous at x = 5.    Answer:  LHL = f(5) = 5k + 1. RHL = 15 - 5 = 10. 5k + 1 = 10 gives  k = 9/5 .

title: Q30 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q30. (MCQ, 2025)  f(x) = |x| + |x - 1|. Then at x = 0 and x = 1, f is: (C) continuous but not differentiable.    Answer: (C).  Modulus functions are continuous everywhere but have sharp corners where the inside is 0.

title: Q31 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q31. (2 marks, 2024)  Is f(x) = x²|x| differentiable at x = 0?    Answer:  f(x) = x³ for x ≥ 0 and -x³ for x < 0. LHD = lim (h→0) [-(-h)³ - 0]/(-h) = lim h³/(-h) = 0. RHD = lim h³/h = 0. LHD = RHD = 0, so  differentiable at x = 0 .

title: Q32 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q32. ★ (3-5 marks, 2024 and 2025)  If √(1 - x²) + √(1 - y²) = a(x - y), prove dy/dx = √[(1 - y²)/(1 - x²)].    Answer:      Put x = sin A, y = sin B. Then cos A + cos B = a(sin A - sin B).   2 cos((A+B)/2) cos((A-B)/2) = a × 2 cos((A+B)/2) sin((A-B)/2).   Cancel: cot((A - B)/2) = a, so A - B = 2 cot⁻¹a (a constant).   sin⁻¹x - sin⁻¹y = 2 cot⁻¹a. Differentiate: 1/√(1 - x²) - (1/√(1 - y²)) dy/dx = 0.    dy/dx = √(1 - y²)/√(1 - x²) .

title: Q33 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q33. (3 marks, 2024)  If y = (tan x)ˣ, find dy/dx.    Answer:  log y = x log(tan x). Differentiate: (1/y) dy/dx = log(tan x) + x × (sec²x / tan x).  dy/dx = (tan x)ˣ [log(tan x) + x sec²x / tan x]  (= (tan x)ˣ [log tan x + 2x / sin 2x]).

title: Q34 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q34. (3 marks, SQP)  If x = sin³t, y = cos³t, find d²y/dx² at t = π/4.    Answer:  dx/dt = 3 sin²t cos t, dy/dt = -3 cos²t sin t, so dy/dx = -cot t. d²y/dx² = (d/dt of -cot t) × dt/dx = cosec²t / (3 sin²t cos t) = 1/(3 sin⁴t cos t). At t = π/4: sin⁴t = 1/4, cos t = 1/√2: d²y/dx² = 1/(3 × 1/4 × 1/√2) =  4√2/3 .

title: Q35 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q35. (3 marks, 2019)  If y = (sin⁻¹x)², prove (1 - x²) d²y/dx² - x dy/dx - 2 = 0.    Answer:  y1 = 2 sin⁻¹x / √(1 - x²), so √(1 - x²) y1 = 2 sin⁻¹x. Square: (1 - x²) y1² = 4y. Differentiate: (1 - x²) 2y1y2 - 2x y1² = 4y1. Divide by 2y1:  (1 - x²) y2 - x y1 = 2 . Hence proved.

title: Q36 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q36. (2 marks, 2025)  If tan⁻¹(x² + y²) = a², find dy/dx.    Answer:  x² + y² = tan(a²), a constant. Differentiate: 2x + 2y dy/dx = 0,  dy/dx = -x/y .

title: Q37 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q37. (2 marks, SQP)  If y = sin(x + y), and dy/dx = 0, prove y = ±1.    Answer:  dy/dx = cos(x + y)(1 + dy/dx), so dy/dx (1 - cos(x + y)) = cos(x + y). If dy/dx = 0, cos(x + y) = 0, so sin(x + y) = ±1, i.e.  y = ±1 .

title: Q38 · Chapter 5: Continuity and Differentiability
text: Q38. (MCQ, SQP)  Derivative of cos⁻¹(2x² - 1) with respect to cos⁻¹x is:  2 .  Reason:  Put x = cos u: cos⁻¹(2cos²u - 1) = cos⁻¹(cos 2u) = 2u, and d(2u)/du = 2.

title: Q39 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q39. ★ (3 marks, SQP)  The circular area of vision on the ground of a surveillance drone increases at the rate of 44 m² per metre as it gains height. The radius of the circle increases at 6 m/s. Find the rate at which the height of the drone increases when the radius is 14 m. (Use π = 22/7.)    Answer:      Area A = πr². dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 6 =  528 m²/s .   Given dA/dh = 44 m² per metre.   dA/dt = (dA/dh) × (dh/dt), so 528 = 44 × dh/dt.    dh/dt = 12 m/s.

title: Q40 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q40. ★ (2 marks, 2026)  A room-freshener bottle is an inverted cone. The volume of perfume decreases at a steady 1 mm³/min. Find the rate at which the level of perfume is dropping when the level is 10 mm, if the semi-vertical angle of the cone is π/6.    Answer:      r = h tan(π/6) = h/√3.   V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(h²/3)h = πh³/9.   dV/dt = (πh²/3) dh/dt. Put dV/dt = -1, h = 10: -1 = (100π/3) dh/dt.   dh/dt = -3/(100π). The level is  dropping at 3/(100π) mm/min .

title: Q41 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q41. (Case study 4 marks, 2023)  A conical tank (semi-vertical angle 45°) is full of water. Water drips out at a uniform rate of 2 cm³/s. (i) Find the volume in terms of radius r. (ii) Find the rate of change of radius when r = 2√2 cm. (iii) Find the rate at which the wet surface is decreasing when r = 2√2 cm.    Answer:      (i) Angle 45°, so h = r.  V = (1/3)πr²h = πr³/3.    (ii) dV/dt = πr² dr/dt = -2. At r = 2√2: r² = 8, so dr/dt = -2/(8π) =  -1/(4π) cm/s .   (iii) Wet surface = curved surface S = πrl, where l = √(r² + h²) = r√2. So S = √2 πr².   dS/dt = 2√2 πr × dr/dt = 2√2 π × 2√2 × (-1/(4π)) = -2.  Decreasing at 2 cm²/s.

title: Q42 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q42. (2 marks, practice)  The side of an equilateral triangle increases at 3 cm/s. How fast is its area increasing when the side is 15 cm?    Answer:  A = (√3/4)a². dA/dt = (√3/2) a × da/dt = (√3/2) × 15 × 3 =  45√3/2 cm²/s .

title: Q43 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q43. (3 marks, practice, NCERT type)  Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of f(x) = 2x³ - 15x² + 36x + 1 on [1, 5].    Answer:      f'(x) = 6x² - 30x + 36 = 6(x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 2, 3 (critical points).   Check critical points and end points: f(1) = 24, f(2) = 29, f(3) = 28, f(5) = 56.    Absolute maximum = 56 at x = 5; absolute minimum = 24 at x = 1.

title: Q44 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q44. (4 marks, practice)  A farmer has 300 m of fencing. He wants to fence a rectangular field and also put one partition fence inside it, parallel to one side. Find the largest area he can enclose.    Answer:      Let the side parallel to the partition be x (there are 3 of these) and the other side y (2 of these). 3x + 2y = 300, so y = (300 - 3x)/2.   Area A = xy = (300x - 3x²)/2.   dA/dx = (300 - 6x)/2 = 0 gives x = 50. d²A/dx² = -3 < 0, so maximum.   y = (300 - 150)/2 = 75.  Maximum area = 50 × 75 = 3750 m².

title: Q45 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q45. ★ (Case study 4 marks, 2026)  A delivery company has 5000 subscribers paying ₹300 a year. For every ₹1 increase, 10 subscribers leave. The fee is increased by ₹x. (i) How many leave? (ii) Write revenue R(x). (iii) Find x for maximum R(x), and where R is increasing / decreasing.    Answer:      (i)  10x subscribers  leave.   (ii)  R(x) = (5000 - 10x)(300 + x).    (iii) R'(x) = -10(300 + x) + (5000 - 10x) = 2000 - 20x = 0, so  x = 100 . R''(x) = -20 < 0, so maximum. (Maximum revenue = 4000 × 400 = ₹16,00,000.)   R'(x) > 0 for x < 100 and < 0 for x > 100:  increasing on (0, 100), decreasing on (100, 5000) .

title: Q46 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q46. ★ (Case study 4 marks, SQP)  Water Quality Index W(x) = 35 + 1.6x - 0.02x², where x = investment in ₹ crore. (i) Find x at the stationary point. (ii) Find the maximum WQI using the second derivative test. (iii) Find W(35) and W(60) and compare with the maximum.    Answer:      (i) W'(x) = 1.6 - 0.04x = 0, so  x = 40 .   (ii) W''(x) = -0.04 < 0, so maximum. W(40) = 35 + 64 - 32 =  67 .   (iii) W(35) = 35 + 56 - 24.5 = 66.5, which is  0.5 short  of the maximum. W(60) = 35 + 96 - 72 =  59  < 67, so spending beyond ₹40 crore gives a  diminishing return .

title: Q47 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q47. (Short answer, 2018)  Total cost C(x) = 0.005x³ - 0.02x² + 30x + 5000. Find the marginal cost when 3 units are produced.    Answer:  Marginal cost = C'(x) = 0.015x² - 0.04x + 30. C'(3) = 0.135 - 0.12 + 30 =  ₹30.015 .

title: Q48 · Chapter 6: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
text: Q48. (MCQ, 2026C)  The values of x for which the rate of increase of f(x) = x³ - 5x² + 6x - 7 is thrice the rate of increase of x are:    Answer: x = 3 and x = 1/3.  df/dt = (3x² - 10x + 6) dx/dt = 3 dx/dt, so 3x² - 10x + 3 = 0, (3x - 1)(x - 3) = 0.

title: Q49 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q49. ★ (3 marks, 2026)  Evaluate ∫₀¹ x tan⁻¹x dx.    Answer:  By parts (u = tan⁻¹x, v' = x):     = [(x²/2) tan⁻¹x]₀¹ - ∫₀¹ (x²/2) × 1/(1 + x²) dx   = π/8 - (1/2)∫₀¹ [1 - 1/(1 + x²)] dx = π/8 - (1/2)[x - tan⁻¹x]₀¹   = π/8 - (1/2)(1 - π/4) = π/8 - 1/2 + π/8 =  π/4 - 1/2 .

title: Q51 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q51. (3 marks, practice, NCERT)  Find ∫ (x + sin x)/(1 + cos x) dx.    Answer:  1 + cos x = 2cos²(x/2) and sin x = 2 sin(x/2) cos(x/2).     Integral = ∫ (x/2) sec²(x/2) dx + ∫ tan(x/2) dx.   By parts, ∫(x/2) sec²(x/2) dx = x tan(x/2) - ∫ tan(x/2) dx.   The two ∫tan(x/2) dx cancel:  x tan(x/2) + C .

title: Q52 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q52. (5 marks, SQP)  Evaluate ∫ from -a to a of √[(a - x)/(a + x)] dx.    Answer:      Multiply top and bottom by √(a - x): integrand = (a - x)/√(a² - x²) = a/√(a² - x²) - x/√(a² - x²).   The second part is an odd function, so its integral from -a to a is 0.   First part: a × 2∫₀ᵃ dx/√(a² - x²) = 2a [sin⁻¹(x/a)]₀ᵃ = 2a × π/2.    Answer = πa.

title: Q53 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q53. ★ (3 marks, 2026)  If I₁ = ∫ from -π/4 to π/4 of dx/(1 + cos 2x) and I₂ = ∫ from -1/2 to 1/2 of |x| dx, show that I₁ - 4I₂ = 0.    Answer:      1 + cos 2x = 2cos²x, so I₁ = (1/2)∫sec²x dx = (1/2)[tan x] from -π/4 to π/4 = (1/2)(1 + 1) =  1 .   |x| is even: I₂ = 2∫₀^(1/2) x dx = 2 × (1/8) =  1/4 .   I₁ - 4I₂ = 1 - 1 = 0. Hence proved.

title: Q54 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q54. (2 marks, SQP)  Evaluate ∫ dx / (x√(x⁶ - 1)).    Answer:  Put x³ = t, 3x² dx = dt. Integral = ∫ x² dx/(x³√(x⁶ - 1)) = (1/3)∫ dt/(t√(t² - 1)) =  (1/3) sec⁻¹(x³) + C .

title: Q55 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q55. (A-R, SQP)  A: ∫ from -1 to 1 of |x - 2| dx = 4. R: If f(-x) = f(x), then ∫ from -a to a of f(x) dx = 2∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx.    Answer: (B).  On [-1, 1], x - 2 < 0, so ∫(2 - x) dx = [2x - x²/2] from -1 to 1 = 4. A is true. R is a true property, but |x - 2| is not even, so R does not explain A.

title: Q56 · Chapter 7: Integrals
text: Q56. (2 marks, SQP)  Evaluate ∫ (cos x - sin x)/√(sin 2x) dx.    Answer:  Put t = sin x + cos x, dt = (cos x - sin x) dx, and t² = 1 + sin 2x, so sin 2x = t² - 1. Integral = ∫ dt/√(t² - 1) = log|t + √(t² - 1)| =  log|sin x + cos x + √(sin 2x)| + C .

title: Q57 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q57. ★ (5 marks, 2026C; same type 2024)  Using integration, find the area bounded by the ellipse 9x² + 16y² = 144 and the lines x = 2 and x = -2.    Answer:      Ellipse: x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, so y = (3/4)√(16 - x²).   The region is symmetric in all four quarters: Area = 4∫₀² (3/4)√(16 - x²) dx = 3∫₀² √(16 - x²) dx.   ∫√(a² - x²) dx = (x/2)√(a² - x²) + (a²/2) sin⁻¹(x/a).   ∫₀² √(16 - x²) dx = (2/2)√12 + 8 sin⁻¹(1/2) = 2√3 + 8π/6 = 2√3 + 4π/3.    Area = 3(2√3 + 4π/3) = 6√3 + 4π square units.

title: Q58 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q58. ★ (5 marks, 2026C)  Using integration, find the area bounded by the curve y = x² and the line y = 2.    Answer:      They meet where x² = 2, x = ±√2. The region is symmetric about the y-axis.   Area = 2∫₀² x dy = 2∫₀² √y dy = 2 × (2/3)[y^(3/2)]₀² = (4/3) × 2√2.    Area = 8√2/3 square units.

title: Q59 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q59. (3 marks, practice, NCERT)  Sketch y = |x + 3| and evaluate ∫ from -6 to 0 of |x + 3| dx.    Answer:  The graph is a V with its corner at (-3, 0).     ∫ from -6 to -3 of -(x + 3) dx = [-(x + 3)²/2] = 0 + 9/2 = 9/2.   ∫ from -3 to 0 of (x + 3) dx = [(x + 3)²/2] = 9/2.    Total = 9 square units.

title: Q60 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q60. (5 marks, SQP)  Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by y² = 2x and the line x - 2y = 0.    Answer:      Meeting points: y = x/2 in y² = 2x gives x²/4 = 2x, so x = 0 or 8. Points (0, 0) and (8, 4).   Area = ∫₀⁸ [√(2x) - x/2] dx = [√2 × (2/3) x^(3/2) - x²/4]₀⁸ = (2√2/3)(16√2) - 16 = 64/3 - 16.    Area = 16/3 square units.

title: Q61 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q61. (5 marks, SQP)  Find the area of the region {(x, y) : 0 ≤ y ≤ √(4 - x²), x + y ≥ 2}.    Answer:      y = √(4 - x²) is the upper half of the circle x² + y² = 4. The line x + y = 2 meets it at (2, 0) and (0, 2).   Area = ∫₀² √(4 - x²) dx - ∫₀² (2 - x) dx = [quarter circle] - [triangle] = π - 2.    Area = (π - 2) square units.

title: Q62 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q62. (Case study parts, 2026)  A roundabout has boundary C1: x² + y² = 64; a circular pond in its middle is C2: x² + y² = 4. (i) Express y as a function of x for both. (ii) Using integration, find the area of the pond and of the region between the two circles.    Answer:      (i) C1: y = ±√(64 - x²); C2: y = ±√(4 - x²).   (ii) Pond = 4∫₀² √(4 - x²) dx = 4[(x/2)√(4 - x²) + 2 sin⁻¹(x/2)]₀² = 4 × π =  4π sq units .   Big circle = 4∫₀⁸ √(64 - x²) dx = 4 × 16π = 64π. Region between = 64π - 4π =  60π sq units .

title: Q63 · Chapter 8: Application of Integrals (Area)
text: Q63. (MCQ, 2026)  The area bounded by y = x|x|, the x-axis and x = -1, x = 1 is:    Answer: 2/3 sq units.  The curve is odd, so take 2∫₀¹ x² dx = 2/3 (area is always taken positive, never 0).

title: Q64 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q64. ★ (3 marks, SQP)  Find the particular solution of x dy + (y - x²eˣ) dx = 0, given y(1) = 0.    Answer:      Divide by x dx: dy/dx + y/x = x eˣ. Linear, P = 1/x, Q = x eˣ.   IF = e^(∫1/x dx) = x.   Solution: xy = ∫x² eˣ dx = eˣ(x² - 2x + 2) + C.   y(1) = 0: 0 = e(1 - 2 + 2) + C, so C = -e.    xy = eˣ(x² - 2x + 2) - e.

title: Q65 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q65. ★ (3 marks, 2024)  Find the particular solution of x² dy/dx - xy = x² cos²(y/2x), given y = π/2 when x = 1.    Answer:      Divide by x²: dy/dx = y/x + cos²(y/2x). Homogeneous: put y = vx, dy/dx = v + x dv/dx.   v + x dv/dx = v + cos²(v/2), so sec²(v/2) dv = dx/x.   Integrate: 2 tan(v/2) = log|x| + C.   x = 1, v = π/2: 2 tan(π/4) = 0 + C, so C = 2.    2 tan(y/2x) = log|x| + 2.

title: Q66 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q66. (3 marks, practice, NCERT)  Solve eˣ tan y dx + (2 - eˣ) sec²y dy = 0, given y = π/4 when x = 0.    Answer:      Separate: sec²y/tan y dy = eˣ/(eˣ - 2) dx.   Integrate: log|tan y| = log|eˣ - 2| + log|C|, so tan y = C(eˣ - 2).   x = 0, y = π/4: 1 = C(1 - 2), C = -1.    tan y = 2 - eˣ.

title: Q67 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q67. ★ (3 marks, 2026)  Find the general solution of x² dy/dx = x² + xy + y².    Answer:      dy/dx = 1 + y/x + (y/x)². Put y = vx: v + x dv/dx = 1 + v + v².   x dv/dx = 1 + v², so dv/(1 + v²) = dx/x.   tan⁻¹v = log|x| + C.    tan⁻¹(y/x) = log|x| + C.

title: Q68 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q68. (3 marks, 2026)  Find the particular solution of xy dy/dx = (x + 2)(y + 2), given y(1) = -1.    Answer:      Separate: y/(y + 2) dy = (x + 2)/x dx, i.e. [1 - 2/(y + 2)] dy = [1 + 2/x] dx.   Integrate: y - 2 log|y + 2| = x + 2 log|x| + C.   x = 1, y = -1: -1 - 0 = 1 + 0 + C, so C = -2.    y - 2 log|y + 2| = x + 2 log|x| - 2.

title: Q69 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q69. (5 marks, 2026C)  Solve x² dy + y(x + y) dx = 0, given y = 1 when x = 1.    Answer:      dy/dx = -(xy + y²)/x². Put y = vx: v + x dv/dx = -v - v², so x dv/dx = -(v² + 2v).   dv/[v(v + 2)] = -dx/x. Partial fractions: (1/2)[1/v - 1/(v + 2)] dv = -dx/x.   (1/2) log|v/(v + 2)| = -log|x| + log C, so v/(v + 2) = C²/x², i.e. y/(y + 2x) = K/x².   x = 1, y = 1: 1/3 = K.    3x²y = y + 2x  (or y = 2x/(3x² - 1)).

title: Q70 · Chapter 9: Differential Equations
text: Q70. (A-R, SQP)  A: The general solution of a differential equation represents a family of curves. R: The derivative of an arbitrary constant is zero.    Answer: (A)  (as per the official SQP marking scheme): both true, and R is the correct explanation.

title: Q71 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q71. ★ (2 marks, 2026)  Find the vector of magnitude 14 in the direction of QP, where P(1, 3, 2) and Q(-1, 0, 8).    Answer:  QP = P - Q = 2i + 3j - 6k. |QP| = √(4 + 9 + 36) = 7. Unit vector = (2i + 3j - 6k)/7. Required vector = 14 × (2i + 3j - 6k)/7 =  4i + 6j - 12k .

title: Q72 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q72. ★ (2 marks, 2026)  a = 3i - 2j + 2k and b = i + 2k are adjacent sides of a parallelogram. Find its diagonals and their lengths.    Answer:  a + b = 4i - 2j + 4k, length √(16 + 4 + 16) =  6 . a - b = 2i - 2j, length √(4 + 4) =  2√2 .

title: Q73 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q73. (2 marks, SQP)  |a| = √6, a·b = 1 and b × a = 3i + 4j - 2k. Find |b|.    Answer:  |a × b|² + (a·b)² = |a|²|b|². |b × a|² = 9 + 16 + 4 = 29. So 29 + 1 = 6|b|², |b|² = 5,  |b| = √5 .

title: Q74 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q74. ★ (2 marks, 2024)  ABCD is a parallelogram with AB = 2i - 4j + 5k and DB = 3i - 6j + 2k. Find AD and the area of ABCD.    Answer:  AB = AD + DB, so AD = AB - DB =  -i + 2j + 3k . AB × AD = (-12 - 10)i - (6 + 5)j + (4 - 4)k = -22i - 11j + 0k. Area = |AB × AD| = √(484 + 121) = √605 =  11√5 sq units .

title: Q75 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q75. (2 marks, practice)  Find the area of the triangle with adjacent sides a = 2i - j + k and b = i + 3j - k.    Answer:  a × b = (1 - 3)i - (-2 - 1)j + (6 + 1)k = -2i + 3j + 7k. |a × b| = √(4 + 9 + 49) = √62. Area of triangle = (1/2)|a × b| =  √62/2 sq units .

title: Q76 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q76. (MCQ, SQP)  A vector perpendicular to both i + j and i - j is: (A) -2j (B) 3k (C) 2i (D) 2i + k.    Answer: (B).  Both vectors lie in the xy-plane, so any multiple of k is perpendicular to both. (Check: (i + j) × (i - j) = -2k.)

title: Q77 · Chapter 10: Vectors
text: Q77. (2 marks, 2018 type)  Two vectors a and b have the same magnitude, the angle between them is 60° and a·b = 9/2. Find their magnitude.    Answer:  a·b = |a||b| cos 60° = |a|² × 1/2 = 9/2. So |a|² = 9,  |a| = |b| = 3 .

title: Q79 · Chapter 11: Three-dimensional Geometry (lines only)
text: Q79. ★ (3 marks, SQP)  Find the foot of the perpendicular from (2, 1, 4) to the line x - 2 = (2y + 3)/4 = 2 - z. Also find the equation of the line through this foot and (2, 1, 4).    Answer:      Standard form: (x - 2)/1 = (y + 3/2)/2 = (z - 2)/(-1). Any point on it: Q(k + 2, 2k - 3/2, 2 - k).   PQ = (k, 2k - 5/2, -2 - k). PQ is perpendicular to the line: 1(k) + 2(2k - 5/2) - 1(-2 - k) = 6k - 3 = 0, so k = 1/2.    Foot = (5/2, -1/2, 3/2).    Direction of PQ = (1/2, -3/2, -5/2), i.e. (1, -3, -5). Line:  (x - 2)/1 = (y - 1)/(-3) = (z - 4)/(-5) .

title: Q80 · Chapter 11: Three-dimensional Geometry (lines only)
text: Q80. ★ (5 marks, 2024 and 2025)  Find the foot of the perpendicular and the image of A(1, 6, 3) in the line x/1 = (y - 1)/2 = (z - 2)/3.    Answer:      Any point on the line: M(k, 2k + 1, 3k + 2). AM = (k - 1, 2k - 5, 3k - 1).   AM ⊥ line: (k - 1) + 2(2k - 5) + 3(3k - 1) = 14k - 14 = 0, so k = 1.    Foot M = (1, 3, 5).    M is the mid-point of A and its image A'(x, y, z): (1 + x)/2 = 1, (6 + y)/2 = 3, (3 + z)/2 = 5.    Image A' = (1, 0, 7).  (In 2024 it was asked the other way: "the image of P is (1, 0, 7), find P". Same working.)

title: Q81 · Chapter 11: Three-dimensional Geometry (lines only)
text: Q81. (3 marks, practice, NCERT)  Find the distance between the parallel lines r = i + 2j - 4k + λ(2i + 3j + 6k) and r = 3i + 3j - 5k + μ(2i + 3j + 6k).    Answer:      b = 2i + 3j + 6k, |b| = 7. a2 - a1 = 2i + j - k.   b × (a2 - a1) = (3(-1) - 6(1))i - (2(-1) - 6(2))j + (2(1) - 3(2))k = -9i + 14j - 4k.   |b × (a2 - a1)| = √(81 + 196 + 16) = √293.    Distance = √293/7 units.

title: Q82 · Chapter 11: Three-dimensional Geometry (lines only)
text: Q82. (Case study 4 marks, SQP)  Laser beams: l1: r = (λ + 1)i + (3λ + 2)j + (3 - λ)k; l2: r = 2(μ + 1)i + (3μ - 1)j + (μ + 1)k; l3: r = (γ + 3)i + (3γ - 1)j + (1 - γ)k. (i) Show l1 and l2 are not parallel. (ii) Show l1 and l3 are parallel. (iii) Find the shortest distance between l1 and l2.    Answer:      Rewrite: l1: a1 = (1, 2, 3), b1 = (1, 3, -1); l2: a2 = (2, -1, 1), b2 = (2, 3, 1); l3: a3 = (3, -1, 1), b3 = (1, 3, -1).   (i) 1/2 ≠ 3/3, so b1 and b2 are not proportional:  not parallel .   (ii) b3 = b1, so  l1 ∥ l3 .   (iii) b1 × b2 = (3 + 3)i - (1 + 2)j + (3 - 6)k = 6i - 3j - 3k, |b1 × b2| = √54 = 3√6. a2 - a1 = (1, -3, -2). Dot = 6 + 9 + 6 = 21.    SD = 21/(3√6) = 7/√6 units.  (OR part, l1 and l3: b1 × (a3 - a1) = -9i + 0j - 9k, SD = 9√2/√11 units.)

title: Q83 · Chapter 11: Three-dimensional Geometry (lines only)
text: Q83. (2 marks, SQP)  The line through (2, 6, 5) and (3, p, 7) is parallel to the line through (-4, 3, 4) and (-1, 0, q). Find q/p.    Answer:  Direction ratios: (1, p - 6, 2) and (3, -3, q - 4). Parallel, so 1/3 = (p - 6)/(-3) = 2/(q - 4). Hence p - 6 = -1,  p = 5 ; q - 4 = 6,  q = 10 .  q/p = 2.

title: Q84 · Chapter 12: Linear Programming
text: Q84. ★ (3 marks, SQP)  Maximise Z = 40x + 30y subject to x + y ≤ 6, 2x ≥ y, y ≥ 2.    Answer:      Lines: x + y = 6, y = 2x, y = 2. The feasible region is the triangle bounded by them.   Corners: y = 2 and y = 2x: (1, 2); y = 2 and x + y = 6: (4, 2); y = 2x and x + y = 6: (2, 4).   Z(1, 2) = 100, Z(4, 2) = 220, Z(2, 4) = 200.    Maximum Z = 220 at (4, 2).

title: Q85 · Chapter 12: Linear Programming
text: Q85. ★ (3 marks, 2026)  Minimise Z = 13x - 15y subject to x + y ≤ 7, 2x - 3y + 6 ≥ 0, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.    Answer:      Lines: x + y = 7 through (7, 0), (0, 7); 2x - 3y + 6 = 0 through (-3, 0), (0, 2). (0, 0) satisfies both.   Corners: (0, 0), (7, 0), (3, 4) [solving x + y = 7 and 2x - 3y = -6], (0, 2).   Z: (0, 0) = 0; (7, 0) = 91; (3, 4) = 39 - 60 = -21; (0, 2) = -30.    Minimum Z = -30 at (0, 2).  (The maximum, 91 at (7, 0), is also often asked.)

title: Q86 · Chapter 12: Linear Programming
text: Q86. ★ (4 marks, 2020)  A furniture trader has ₹50,000 to invest and space for at most 35 items. A chair costs ₹1000, a table ₹2000. Profit: ₹150 per chair, ₹250 per table. Formulate as an LPP and maximise profit.    Answer:      Let x chairs, y tables. Maximise Z = 150x + 250y.   Constraints: 1000x + 2000y ≤ 50000, i.e. x + 2y ≤ 50; x + y ≤ 35; x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.   Corners: (0, 0), (35, 0), (20, 15) [solving x + 2y = 50, x + y = 35], (0, 25).   Z: 0, 5250, 6750, 6250.    Maximum profit ₹6750 with 20 chairs and 15 tables.

title: Q89 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q89. ★ (3 marks, 2026)  Bag I has 3 red and 4 white balls; bag II has 8 red and 6 white. A die is thrown: if it shows a number less than 3, a ball is drawn from bag I, otherwise from bag II. Find the probability that the ball is red.    Answer:      P(E1) = P(die < 3) = 2/6 = 1/3; P(E2) = 2/3.   P(red | E1) = 3/7; P(red | E2) = 8/14 = 4/7.   P(red) = (1/3)(3/7) + (2/3)(4/7) = 3/21 + 8/21 =  11/21 .

title: Q90 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q90. ★ (5 marks, SQP)  Users of a fitness app: Alpha 45%, Beta 30%, Gamma 15%, Delta 10%. Chance of a false heart-rate alert: 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.01. (i) Find P(false alert). (ii) If a false alert occurs, find the probability it came from Beta.    Answer:      (i) P(F) = 0.45(0.01) + 0.30(0.02) + 0.15(0.05) + 0.10(0.01) = 0.0045 + 0.006 + 0.0075 + 0.001 =  0.019 .   (ii) P(Beta | F) = 0.006/0.019 =  6/19 .

title: Q91 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q91. ★ (Case study 4 marks, 2024)  Severe, moderate and light turbulence are equally likely. The chance of a late arrival is 55%, 37% and 17% respectively. (i) Find P(late). (ii) If late, find the probability it was due to moderate turbulence.    Answer:      (i) P(L) = (1/3)(0.55 + 0.37 + 0.17) = 1.09/3 =  109/300 .   (ii) P(moderate | L) = (1/3)(0.37) / (109/300) = (37/300)/(109/300) =  37/109 .

title: Q92 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q92. ★ (Long answer, 2019)  Operators A, B, C produce 1%, 5%, 7% defective items and work 50%, 30%, 20% of the time. An item is found defective. Find the probability it was produced by A.    Answer:      P(D) = 0.5(0.01) + 0.3(0.05) + 0.2(0.07) = 0.005 + 0.015 + 0.014 = 0.034.   P(A | D) = 0.005/0.034 =  5/34 .

title: Q93 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q93. (4 marks, 2020)  Bag I has 3 red, 5 black; bag II has 4 red, 3 black. One ball is moved from bag I to bag II, then a ball is drawn from bag II. It is black. Find the probability that the moved ball was black.    Answer:      E1: red moved, P = 3/8 → bag II has 5R, 3B, P(black) = 3/8.   E2: black moved, P = 5/8 → bag II has 4R, 4B, P(black) = 4/8.   P(black) = (3/8)(3/8) + (5/8)(4/8) = 9/64 + 20/64 = 29/64.   P(E2 | black) = (20/64)/(29/64) =  20/29 .

title: Q94 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q94. (2 marks, 2022)  A pair of dice is thrown. The sum is even. Find the probability that at least one die shows 3.    Answer:  Even-sum outcomes = 18. Of these, with a 3: (3,1), (3,3), (3,5), (1,3), (5,3) = 5.  P = 5/18.

title: Q95 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q95. (2 marks, 2022)  A and B solve a problem with probabilities 2/3 and 3/5, independently. Find the probability that the problem is solved.    Answer:  P(not solved) = (1/3)(2/5) = 2/15.  P(solved) = 1 - 2/15 = 13/15.

title: Q96 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q96. (MCQ, SQP)  A and B are independent, P(A) = 1/6, P(B) = k. P(exactly one occurs) = 1/3. Find k. (A) 1/4 (B) 2/3 (C) 3/4 (D) 5/6.    Answer: (A).  P(A)P(B') + P(A')P(B) = (1/6)(1 - k) + (5/6)k = 1/3 → 1/6 + 4k/6 = 2/6 →  k = 1/4 .

title: Q97 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q97. (MCQ, SQP)  A die is thrown twice. Find the probability that at least one number is 4, given that the sum is a multiple of 5.    Answer: 4/7.  Sum 5 or 10: (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1), (4,6), (5,5), (6,4) = 7 outcomes. With a 4: (1,4), (4,1), (4,6), (6,4) = 4.

title: Q98 · Chapter 13: Probability
text: Q98. (MCQ, SQP)  The probability of rain on a day is 1/5, independent of other days. The probability of rain on three consecutive days is:  (D) 1/125  = (1/5)³.

title: 1. Exam at a glance (2026-27)
text: 1. Exam at a glance (2026-27)          Item   Detail           Theory paper   70 marks, 3 hours (+15 minutes reading time)       Practical exam   30 marks (school + external examiner)       Total   100 marks       Number of questions   33, all compulsory, about 33% internal choice       Section A   Q1–16: 16 × 1 mark (12 MCQs + 4 Assertion–Reason) = 16 marks       Section B   Q17–21: 5 × 2 marks (very short answer) = 10 marks       Section C   Q22–28: 7 × 3 marks (short answer) = 21 marks       Section D   Q29–30: 2 × 4 marks (case-based, with choice in one part) = 8 marks       Section E   Q31–33: 3 × 5 marks (long answer, full OR choice) = 15 marks       What is tested   50% knowledge & understanding, 30% application, 20% analyse/evaluate        Pass rule (Class XII)     33% in theory AND 33% in practical, separately  (and 33% overall)       Marks needed in theory   33% of 70 = 23.1 →  at least 24 out of 70        Marks needed in practical   33% of 30 = 9.9 →  at least 10 out of 30          CBSE note on the 2026-27 SQP: "There is no change in the Question Paper Design and Assessment Pattern for Academic Session 2026-27."    Practical (30 marks) break-up:  one major experiment 5, one minor experiment 4, slide preparation 5, spotting 7, practical record + viva 4, investigatory project + project viva 5. Most students who attend practicals and keep a complete file get 20+ out of 30.  Never miss the practical exam  — failing practical alone means failing the subject.

title: 2. Unit / chapter weightage (2026-27)
text: 2. Unit / chapter weightage (2026-27)    Official unit marks (CBSE curriculum 2026-27):         Unit   Chapters (NCERT XII)   Marks           VI Reproduction   1 Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants; 2 Human Reproduction; 3 Reproductive Health    16        VII Genetics and Evolution   4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation; 5 Molecular Basis of Inheritance; 6 Evolution    20        VIII Biology and Human Welfare   7 Human Health and Disease; 8 Microbes in Human Welfare    12        IX Biotechnology and its Applications   9 Biotechnology – Principles and Processes; 10 Biotechnology and its Applications    12        X Ecology and Environment   11 Organisms and Populations; 12 Ecosystem; 13 Biodiversity and its Conservation    10            Total     70          CBSE does not give marks chapter by chapter. The table below is  my estimate  from how the 2026-27 SQP divides its 70 marks (it changes a little every year):         Chapter   Approx. marks in SQP 2026-27           1 Flowering plants   ~6       2 Human reproduction   ~6       3 Reproductive health   ~4       4 Inheritance & variation   ~8       5 Molecular basis of inheritance   ~9       6 Evolution   ~3       7 Human health & disease   ~6       8 Microbes   ~6       9 + 10 Biotechnology   ~12       11 + 12 + 13 Ecology   ~10 (Q33 has a choice between biodiversity and decomposition)          NOT for the board theory exam (do not waste time):      "Environmental Issues" (pollution, ozone, global warming, etc.) — CBSE says it is assessed  only formatively  (in school), not in the board paper.   Old chapters removed after 2022: Reproduction in Organisms, Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production (animal husbandry, MOET, bee-keeping, plant breeding varieties, SCP), ecological succession, nutrient cycles (phosphorus cycle), organisms & environment (regulators/conformers, adaptations), DDT biomagnification, eutrophication. Old papers (2015–2020) have many such questions — skip them.   (One exception to watch: the 2026-27 SQP has one Assertion–Reason on tissue culture/totipotency, and the 2026 board paper asked about a virus-free sugarcane plant. Learn the one-line answer given in Q37 below; do not study the whole old chapter.)

title: 3. The 33-mark plan (how to pass safely)
text: 3. The 33-mark plan (how to pass safely)     Goal:  24 out of 70 is the pass mark in theory. We aim for  about 30 (≈43%)  so that a bad day still leaves you above 24.    Why these chapters first?  They are short, mostly "name / list / define / give example" type, and the same questions repeat almost every year.         Order   Chapter(s)   Why easy   Your target marks           1   Ch 7 Human Health and Disease   Diseases table, immunity, AIDS, drugs — pure memory, asked every year   5       2   Ch 8 Microbes in Human Welfare   Microbe → product table, sewage, biogas, biocontrol — asked every year   4       3   Ch 3 Reproductive Health   Contraceptives, MTP, ART (IVF/ZIFT/GIFT), amniocentesis — short and repeated   3       4   Ch 9 + 10 Biotechnology   Same 10 questions repeat: EcoRI, pBR322, PCR, gel electrophoresis, insulin, Bt cotton, RNAi, gene therapy   5       5   Ch 4 Principles of Inheritance   Crosses follow fixed steps (test cross, snapdragon, blood group, haemophilia); disorders table   4       6   Ch 2 Human Reproduction   Diagrams + menstrual cycle + fertilisation/implantation   3       7   Ch 13 Biodiversity + Ch 11 Populations   Evil quartet, in-situ/ex-situ, interactions table   5       8   Ch 1 Flowering plants   Embryo sac diagram, outbreeding devices, double fertilisation, apomixis   2           Total target        31          Extra marks without extra chapters: in Section A,  attempt all 16 MCQs/A-R  — there is no negative marking. Even guessing among 4 options gives you a chance.    Leave for last (only if time):  Ch 5 Molecular Basis (long and tricky — but learn the 1-mark facts and the replication fork / transcription unit diagrams), Ch 6 Evolution (learn homologous vs analogous, Hardy-Weinberg equation, human evolution order), Ch 12 Ecosystem (learn GPP/NPP, pyramids, decomposition steps).    How practicals help:  practical marks are counted separately (you need 10/30), but they also add to the total. A student with 24/30 in practical needs only to cross 24/70 in theory — and has a comfortable overall total. Keep the practical file complete and the project ready; learn the viva questions on pollen germination, mitosis in onion root tip, quadrat method and DNA isolation (Section 6).

title: 4. Previous year question (PYQ) trends, 2015–2026
text: 4.
